bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "California State Motor Vehicle and Engine Pollution Control Standards; Heavy-Duty Vehicle and Engine Emission Warranty and Maintenance Provisions; Advanced Clean Trucks; Zero Emission Airport Shuttle; Zero-Emission Power Train Certification; Waiver of Preemption; Notice of Decision".
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the Environmental Protection Agency notice titled California State Motor Vehicle and Engine Pollution Control Standards; Heavy-Duty Vehicle and Engine Emission Warranty and Maintenance Provisions; Advanced Clean Trucks; Zero Emission Airport Shuttle; Zero-Emission Power Train Certification; Waiver of Preemption; Notice of Decision (88 Fed. Reg. 20688) and published on April 6, 2023. Among other elements, the notice grants the California Air Resources Board request for a waiver several of its regulations, including the Heavy-Duty Vehicle and Engine Emission Warranty Regulations and Maintenance Provisions. (Under the Clean Air Act, California may seek waivers of the preemption prohibiting states from enacting certain emission standards.)

classification.plainSummary: This resolution would block an Environmental Protection Agency decision that allowed California to enforce its own stricter emission standards for heavy-duty trucks and engines. The EPA had granted California a waiver from federal preemption rules, permitting the state to require cleaner trucks, zero-emission airport shuttles, and advanced clean truck standards. If passed, the resolution would nullify that waiver and prevent California from implementing these regulations.

industries.rationale: The resolution directly affects heavy-duty vehicle manufacturers, trucking companies, and motor carriers by determining whether they must comply with California's stricter emission standards.
Automotive and engine manufacturers would face different regulatory requirements depending on whether California's waiver stands or is nullified.
Zero-emission vehicle mandates affect demand for electric vehicle charging infrastructure and clean energy services for commercial fleets.
Requirements for zero-emission trucks and airport shuttles would influence electricity demand and infrastructure investment for fleet charging.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
